sources.title: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis: Lesotho, May 2025-March 2026
sources.organization: Lesotho Vulnerability Assessment Committee (LVAC); Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)
sources.temporal_coverage: IPC analysis of acute food insecurity for May 2025-March 2026, with current and projected periods as defined in the report.
sources.methodology: The LVAC/IPC analysis classifies acute food insecurity; its official indexed PDF excerpt reports high evidence level.
sources.limitations: Direct PDF retrieval timed out; claims use only substantive excerpts indexed from the official LVAC report. Forecast periods have ended; outcomes were not checked.

sources.title: Lesotho: El Niño-Related Drought, Office of the Resident Coordinator Situation Update 04
sources.organization: United Nations Office of the Resident Coordinator in Lesotho; Humanitarian Country Team
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation update covering 16 May-25 July 2016 during the El Niño-related drought.
sources.methodology: Humanitarian Country Team situation update drawing on LVAC, protection assessments and partner reporting.
sources.limitations: A time-specific 2016 emergency report; some protection data were incomplete and do not establish current prevalence.

sources.title: United Nations Lesotho Annual Report 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Lesotho
sources.methodology: UNCT annual results report compiling reported agency and partner activities and outputs.
sources.limitations: Reported outputs are not an independent evaluation of effectiveness or longer-term resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Lesotho Launches IACoV Phase II to Strengthen Climate Resilience and Food Security
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Lesotho
sources.temporal_coverage: UN account of the IACoV Phase II launch and project design on 2 March 2026.
sources.methodology: UN publication summarizing project design, district targeting and launch remarks.
sources.limitations: Project plans and launch claims are not an independent evaluation; Phase II intentions are not treated as delivered results.

claims.locator: Official indexed PDF excerpt, current acute food insecurity, May-September 2025
claims.paraphrase: The analysis classified more than 258,000 rural residents in IPC Phase 3 or above during May-September 2025, a period that had ended by this review.
claims.limitations: This is a dated IPC classification, not a measure of food insecurity in October 2026.

claims.locator: Official indexed PDF excerpt, projected acute food insecurity, October 2025-March 2026
claims.paraphrase: LVAC/IPC projected 334,000 people in Phase 3 or above nationally for October 2025-March 2026; the projection period has since elapsed.
claims.scenario: Source does not specify a climate scenario; this is an IPC food-security projection for October 2025-March 2026.
claims.limitations: Forecast only; no subsequent outcome verification was reviewed.

claims.locator: Official indexed PDF excerpt, key drivers of acute food insecurity
claims.paraphrase: The assessment attributes 2024/25 crop failure to high temperatures and dry spells during a critical growth period; it also lists high food prices and livestock disease among food-insecurity drivers.
claims.limitations: The report also identifies non-climate drivers; this claim does not attribute food insecurity to climate alone.

claims.locator: PDF p.4 (one-based), gender analysis of tensions around livestock and household water; water-point queues
claims.paraphrase: The report describes disputes at water points and gender-differentiated tensions around livestock water and household water collection in drought-affected districts.
claims.limitations: The 2016 analysis is not a current conflict-prevalence estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The gender analysis explicitly links the emergence of social tensions and conflict to the El Niño drought.

claims.locator: PDF p.4 (one-based), child-protection assessment and longer-distance water collection
claims.paraphrase: The report says children collecting water or food at community points, and children walking longer distances during drought, faced increased danger and injury risk.
claims.limitations: The report presents assessed risks, not measured later incidents or current rates.

claims.locator: PDF pp.20-21 (one-based), output 2.3 natural-resource management and output 2.4 resilience and climate action
claims.paraphrase: The UN reported 2025 support for restoration in degraded areas of Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing, including agroforestry, 400 indigenous trees and a check dam; it also reported drought anticipatory-action protocols and improved early-warning procedures for the DMA.
claims.limitations: These are UN-reported 2025 outputs; the report does not independently evaluate their effects.

claims.locator: Paragraphs describing district selection and local climate/food-security conditions
claims.paraphrase: The UN identifies Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing in the Southern Lowlands as facing recurrent drought and land degradation that undermine farming; Thaba-Tseka in the Highlands faces drought, erosion and limited services alongside high poverty and chronic malnutrition.
claims.limitations: The article summarizes district selection for a project, not a comparative district risk assessment.

claims.locator: Paragraphs on Phase I accomplishments and IACoV Phase II design
claims.paraphrase: The UN reports Phase I strengthened national climate-information systems, supported climate-smart agriculture and community risk knowledge; Phase II is funded for US$10 million, implemented by WFP and executed by two ministries.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition
claims.limitations: Phase I results are summarized by the UN launch article; this is not an independent evaluation.

claims.locator: Phase II activities and priority populations
claims.paraphrase: Phase II plans better seasonal forecasts, gender-responsive last-mile climate services, anticipatory action, ecosystem rehabilitation, livelihood diversification and improved market links; it prioritizes women-headed households, youth, persons with disabilities and remote rural communities.
claims.limitations: These are project design commitments, not verified implementation or outcomes.

access_audit.locator: Official PDF indexed excerpts on May-September 2025 classifications, October 2025-March 2026 projection and key drivers inspected; direct PDF open timed out.
access_audit.notes: No claim is based only on document metadata; extracted report passages were available from the official LVAC PDF index. Outcomes after the projection periods were not reviewed.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 8-page Situation Update inspected, especially PDF pp.2-4 on food/water stress, protection and gendered water-point conflict.
access_audit.notes: 2016 El Niño emergency evidence; incomplete population data and dated risk estimates are not treated as current.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full UNCT Annual Report inspected, PDF pp.20-21 on ecosystem restoration, DMA early warning, drought protocols and climate resilience outputs.
access_audit.notes: Report covers 2025 UN and partner activities; outputs are self-reported rather than independently impact-evaluated.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full UN launch article inspected, including district selection, Phase I summary and Phase II implementation design.
access_audit.notes: Launch article reports project design and progress; commitments are not treated as delivered outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: WFP evaluation landing page inspected; linked 3.76 MB evaluation PDF could not be retrieved in this workflow.
access_audit.notes: Landing page verifies evaluation period October 2020-August 2025, criteria, mixed-methods approach and focus on Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing; no evaluation findings are asserted.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; no substantive evaluation claims used.

search_audit.query: Lesotho 2025-26 IPC food insecurity, dry spells and named district exposure primary government and UN reports
search_audit.outcome: Official LVAC/IPC excerpts give 2025-26 national classifications and climate-related drivers; the UN IACoV launch identifies four target districts with differentiated drought, erosion, service and food-security pressures.

search_audit.query: Lesotho El Nino drought water point conflict gendered tension and child protection primary UN assessment
search_audit.outcome: The 2016 Humanitarian Country Team situation update explicitly links drought with gendered social tensions and conflict at water points and describes increased danger for children collecting water or food; these are historical assessed mechanisms, not current incidence estimates.

search_audit.query: Lesotho official reports whether conflict or insecurity obstructed climate adaptation, drought response or access to climate services
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed UN and WFP materials did not establish that FCV or insecurity prevented delivery of a named adaptation activity. The 2016 report describes drought-related water-point conflict; this does not establish a reverse conflict-to-climate-capacity link.

search_audit.query: Lesotho IACoV district resilience, climate information, drought early warning and local restoration government UN reports
search_audit.outcome: UNCT reports 2025 restoration and DMA early-warning outputs; the March 2026 UN launch reports Phase I accomplishments and Phase II commitments for climate forecasting, last-mile services and local adaptation. WFP's independent evaluation PDF was not retrievable, so no findings from it are used.

gaps: The official LVAC/IPC PDF endpoint timed out; the national food-security classifications and drivers rely on substantive official indexed PDF excerpts rather than direct full-PDF retrieval.
The 2025/2026 IPC projection period ended by the 27 October 2026 access date; this extraction does not establish the realized outcome or current food insecurity level.

The 2016 drought report gives a direct climate-to-tension mechanism but is time-bound and does not establish current conflict incidence. No reviewed source shows that FCV or insecurity blocked a named climate-adaptation activity.

The WFP independent Phase I evaluation landing page was accessible, but its linked report PDF was not; evaluation findings were not used. UN-reported project outputs and launch statements are not independent outcome evaluations.
